$comment: Reviewed policy inputs for the content-scopes/v1 contract generator.
Every value here is either (a) an owner decision recorded in decisions.md, or
(b) an observed fact about currently deployed authorization, cited to a pinned source file.
The generator never infers policy from the spreadsheet's 'API Family' or 'Proposed scope' columns alone.

scopeMap.$comment: D1. Column F labels are DISPLAY labels; these are the proposed machine names.

scopeDescriptions.content.audio.read: Reciters, recitations, audio files, timing/lookup, recitation information and styles.
scopeDescriptions.content.quran.read: Chapters, structure, pages, verses and scripts.
scopeDescriptions.content.hadith.read: Hadith references, text and range counts.
scopeDescriptions.content.translations.read: Translation catalogs, information, verse translations and footnotes.

$comment: Live Content API v4 routes that appear nowhere in the source spreadsheet's 208 rows, but
which existing clients can call today through the gateway's `GET /content/*` wildcard.
Without an entry here they would keep working for legacy clients and be refused for a
granular-only client issued under D5, which would narrow access by omission rather than by
review. See route-reconciliation.md sections 3b and 3c.
These are NOT sheet-derived, so they carry no sourceRows. Their scope assignments are an
owner instruction recorded on 10 September 2026, applying these rules to the route path:
/audio present        -> Audio scope
the word hadith       -> Hadith Scope
/verses present       -> the scope covering verses, which is Quran Scope
/mushafs              -> Quran Scope
translations present  -> Translation Scope
none of the above     -> no assignment; keep legacy-only access
Two readings were needed and are called out on the affected entries:
* There is no separate 'verses' scope in the contract. Quran Scope is the one that covers
'chapters, structure, pages, verses and scripts', so /verses/filter and /mushafs both
resolve to it.
* /resources/word_by_word_translations has no `/translations` path segment; the word
appears inside the segment `word_by_word_translations`. Matched on the word, consistent
with how the hadith rule was expressed.
Every entry is additive in exactly the same way as a sheet-derived operation: the legacy
alternatives stay accepted and the quota buckets stay frozen to the pre-migration set.

'post' is genuinely accepted here today. Migration eligibility must be evaluated against these actual alternatives, never against an assumed scope hierarchy.

deprecatedForNewClients.$comment: D5. Still valid for existing identities; not issuable to new ones once v1 policy is active.

$comment: A5. Quota buckets are snapshotted from today's behavior and are deliberately NOT the
authorization alternatives. Today checkRateLimit() iterates the matched scope list, so
adding granular scopes to authorization would silently add new buckets and could split or
double-charge an aggregate allowance. quotaBuckets freezes the pre-migration bucket set.
Source: src/libs/rate-limit.ts :: checkRateLimit (plus the always-charged global '' bucket).
Scopes that must NOT authorize a user-bound token.
content.reflections.read covers five QuranReflect reads whose upstream response depends on
who is asking. When the gateway forwards a user-bound token, quran-reflect-graph's
OAuth2Strategy resolves the real user from it (apps/quran-reflect-graph/src/auth/
oauth2.strategy.ts returns null only for client-credentials tokens), and the post handler
then passes that user AND user.isAdmin into visibility resolution
(modules/posts/posts.controller.ts findOne -> findOnePopulated(id, user, user?.isAdmin)).
Visibility deliberately permits an owner's drafts and private posts, private-room
membership, and administrator access.
So a user-bound token carrying only this scope would reach more than the public-only access
D3 promises. The gateway cannot narrow that downstream, because it forwards the user's own
token and the user identity is derived from it. The only complete boundary the gateway can
enforce is to refuse to let this scope authorize a user-bound request at all.
A user token that also carries post.read/post or comment.read/comment still authorizes via
that legacy alternative, so existing private access is untouched. Only a request authorized
SOLELY by this scope is refused.
The eight C8 scopes are deliberately NOT listed. Their routes are served by the Content API,
which derives no user from the token and returns the same bytes regardless of caller, so a
user-bound token carrying one of them gains nothing extra. Add a scope here only when user
context can change what the upstream returns.

authContexts.$comment: Distinguishes the public app-credential surface from the user-token surface for the same controller operation.

environmentMap.$comment: Column L values normalized. Branch names and GitHub environment labels are NOT environments; see plan section 6A.

$comment: D4. v1 defines scopes as endpoint-family permissions, not strict data-family isolation.
Quran verse endpoints may still embed translations/tafsirs/audio, and content sync snapshots
may return full resources across content types. Strict isolation requires a different,
field-aware design and a revised migration equivalence; it is not activated by this contract.
A6. C8 is the eight table scopes other than content.reflections.read.
Eligibility is decided per operation by intersecting the client's CURRENT effective scope set
with that operation's observed legacyAnyOf. This is finite and mechanical: it never treats a
'content.' string prefix as authorization and never assumes a parent/child hierarchy.

c8Rule.note: A content.create-only client has no intersection and therefore gains no read successors.

reflectionsRule.note: Eligible only when the client's scopes intersect the legacyAnyOf of ALL five public reflection routes. Narrow clients therefore need post.read AND comment.read. A client holding only the 'post' umbrella does satisfy this, because 'post' is an accepted alternative on all five routes today. 'content' alone never satisfies it.
